title: [All-kit]: Warn when journal timestamps can cause migrations to be skipped
body:
This is for the 0.x release line on `main`, using the `_journal.json` migration format.

When migrations from separate branches are merged, the journal order can get out of sync with the `when` timestamps. For example:

- Branch A generates a migration with `when: 100`.
- Branch B generates one with `when: 200`, then merges and applies it first.
- A merges second. The journal conflict is resolved by appending A after B, but A keeps its original timestamp.

The journal now contains `[B: 200, A: 100]`. The database cutoff is already 200, so the migrator silently skips A. `drizzle-kit check` currently says everything is fine.

This adds a warning when a journal entry's `when` is less than or equal to an earlier entry's timestamp. It identifies both entries so the developer can see which migration could be skipped. It's only a warning, with no change to the exit code, and doesn't need a database connection.

Repro: https://github.com/shaneikennedy/drizzle-test

The repro has valid generated migrations and snapshots, an out-of-order journal, and the actual warning output in the README. `npm run check` runs the patched CLI; `npm run check:upstream` runs the original release against the same files.
